adjudication.rationale: In `packages/lib/constants.ts`, `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is defined as `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, which in TS/JS evaluates to the second string (or undefined), not a boolean. It is then used in boolean contexts like `if (!APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED)` (e.g., `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`). So a non-empty env value like the string "false" would be truthy and thus considered "enabled". This is a real, diff-grounded concern (misleading name/type and truthiness semantics), but it’s not definitively a functional defect since the diff appears to intentionally treat “both secrets present” as the enablement condition.
